stories.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue. The LPG tanker TARA GAS remained on fire and adrift off Oman after an attack that left 11 injured, and US guidance has widened a blockade to cover vessels loading Iranian cargo at sea.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and blockade guidance raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
stories.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have continued through November, with two vessels sunk off Bulgaria and crew injured following an earlier wheat carrier capsizing.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.

stories.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
stories.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January and contested reports of a US-Russia diesel arrangement.
stories.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment and crude export balances.

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations.
stories.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties, documents and vessel positions, and can strand tonnage outside compliant trade.

stories.title: US-China ship fees and port state control friction
stories.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue. A US congressional committee is now urging sanctions over China's detention of Panama-flagged ships.
stories.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees, sanctions or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
stories.latest: A US congressional committee is urging sanctions over China's detention of Panama-flagged ships, escalating the dispute beyond the suspended port fees.
sources: US Committee Urges Sanctions Over China’s Detention of Panama-Flagged Ships

stories.title: Strike threat at LA-Long Beach
stories.what: The Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex is bracing for a strike, with employers warning of severe supply chain disruption if last-ditch talks fail.
stories.why_it_matters: A stoppage at the largest US West Coast gateway would disrupt container flows, berth availability and inland logistics, with knock-on congestion for vessels scheduled to call.
